definition: The use of AI models to analyze source code without executing it, identifying potential bugs, security vulnerabilities, or style issues.
details: AI-assisted static analysis tools extend traditional rule-based static analyzers by using learned models that can catch more nuanced or context-dependent issues in code.

explainer.lead: AI-assisted static code analysis uses models to inspect source code without running it, flagging likely bugs, security vulnerabilities, or style issues. It matters because learned models can catch issues that fixed rules miss.

tiers.eli5: It is like a proofreader who reads your code looking for mistakes, without ever running the program.
tiers.practitioner: Teams layer learned models on top of rule-based analyzers to catch context-dependent problems. A pitfall is that model findings can be noisy, so triage matters.
tiers.paperLevel: AI-assisted static analysis extends traditional rule-based static analyzers with learned models that can catch more nuanced or context-dependent issues. Its scope is issues detectable without executing the code.

explainer.example: A learned analyzer reviews a pull request without executing it and flags a suspicious pattern that the rule-based linter did not catch.
